paper.title_en: Photogalvanic transport of nonreciprocal Cooper-pair fluctuations
paper.abstract_en: We develop a theory of the nonlinear optical and transport responses of two-dimensional noncentrosymmetric superconductors in the fluctuation regime above the transition temperature, encompassing the photogalvanic effect, second-harmonic generation, and the photovoltaic Hall effect. Near the transition these responses are strongly enhanced by preformed Cooper pairs, whose nonreciprocity enters the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau description in two distinct ways: through thermodynamic Lifshitz invariants, which encode an asymmetric pair spectrum, and through kinetic Lifshitz invariants, which encode an asymmetric pair relaxation and are locked to the Langevin noise by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. We derive generalized formulas for the Aslamazov-Larkin and Maki-Thompson channels of the nonlinear current, valid for Gaussian fluctuations at drive frequencies below the scale set by temperature and to linear order in the nonreciprocal perturbations, and reduce them to closed-form dimensionless functions. Circular polarization distinguishes the mechanisms: for reciprocal noise without momentum structure the Aslamazov-Larkin channel is helicity independent and its circular photogalvanic response vanishes for any pair spectrum, whereas the Maki-Thompson channel and the nonreciprocal noise support helicity-odd rectified currents, including a fluctuation photovoltaic Hall current transverse to the strain axis. Applications to Rashba-type ($C_{3v}$) and Ising-type ($D_{3h}$) superconductors show how the point-group symmetry dictates the vector structure of the nonlinear currents, and how polarization analysis together with the frequency and dephasing dependences can separate the individual channels experimentally.
